subject: Dedicated capacity renewal & expansion — Luminar AI forecast + sizing
messages:
From: Suresh Patel <suresh.patel@luminarai.com>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai
Cc: alicia@luminarai.com
Date: Fri, 15 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal planning: expected QPS/token growth + sizing ask

Alex —

Thanks for the heads-up that our renewal window is coming up in March. Per our internal planning (attached spreadsheet), Luminar expects roughly 2.3x token growth across the product surface over the next 12 months as we onboard a new personalization tier and expand streaming to mobile clients. Peak QPS is projected to increase from ~450 to ~1,050 for text generation endpoints; embeddings volume will grow ~1.8x.

Can you recommend reserved pool sizing (GPU counts) and whether we should commit to an annual reserved pool or staggered increases? We care about a predictable 95th percentile latency SLO of <120ms for short-chat requests, and cost predictability — so we’re open to a committed model if the uplift is reasonable. Also please include suggested autoscaling buffer and any suggested KV caching or batching knobs we should apply.

Attached: luminar_forecast_q1-q4_2027.xlsx (forecast + traffic patterns)

Appreciate a succinct recommendation and options so we can take to procurement.

—Suresh
Head of Platform, Luminar AI
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>
To: Suresh Patel <suresh.patel@luminarai.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 18 Jan 2027 10:04:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: expected QPS/token growth + sizing ask

Suresh, thanks — got the forecast and reviewed the patterns. High level recommendations below (summary to take to procurement). Full sizing rationale attached.

Option A — Conservative annual commit (recommended for predictability):
- Reserved pool: 8x NVIDIA A100-equivalent GPUs (or 8x vGPUs of similar throughput)
- Expected steady-state QPS handling: ~1,000 qps for chat generation w/ batching + prefix KV cache.
- Autoscaling buffer: +25% burst pool (on-demand) to cover spiky traffic.
- SLOs: will meet 95p <120ms for 16-token short-chat median when using continuous batching and a 3s batching window; for stricter latency we can reduce batching window with trade-off in cost.

Option B — Growth-friendly ramp (lower upfront commit):
- Reserved pool: 5x A100-equivalent now, add 4x at month 6 based on traffic triggers.
- Includes routing policies to offload non-critical jobs to spot/dedicated-surge.

Operational notes: KV cache hit-rate tuning (we saw ~45–60% gains on similar workloads), prompt batching at the application edge, and a 2–3x token budget uplift to account for personalization expansion.

Pricing guidance: 12-month commit with Option A => ~20% discount versus on-demand; Option B => smaller initial commit discount and a priced ramp. I’ve put numbers in the attached PDF.

I’m attaching proposed_capacity_options.pdf with GPU recommendations, estimated monthly token costs, and a suggested SLA addendum for 95p latency. If you’re happy, we’ll draft a PO and route to Karthik for approvals on the commit and discount.

—Alex Martinez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
attachments: redwood_proposed_capacity_options.pdf
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: alex.martinez@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 Jan 2027 08:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal planning: expected QPS/token growth + sizing ask

Alex / team — adding technical ops perspective from CS on the sizing callouts. TL;DR: Option A is safest for latency-sensitive lanes; Option B works if Luminar accepts small degradation during peak growth and enables our reserved-surge.

A few specifics to include in the final playbook:
- Frontline cache: enable prefix KV caching for 80% of short-chat requests; target hit-rate >50% to reduce tokens served.
- Batching policy: continuous batching with 2.0s target window for standard chat; 0.5s window for high-priority small-message lane (requires dedicated lower-batch pool).
- Quantization: recommend starting with 4-bit quantized model in the reserved pool if Luminar wants cost reduction; evaluate quality on the personalization prompts — we can run a quick AB on 50 prompts in 48 hours.
- Cold-start mitigation: keep a small warm standby instance per shard (approx 10% of pool) for <100ms cold-start SLA impact.

I also flagged that embeddings growth may push token storage and retention costs; we should confirm their retention policy so our cost model is accurate.

—Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.ai>

Requested commercial: 12-month reserved pool (8x GPU) with 20% commit discount, 25% burst capacity on-demand, and an SLA addendum matching 95p latency target. Estimated uplift to ARR: $1.1M annualized (numbers in attached pricing sheet).

Can you approve the discount and the SLA phrasing so I can send the PO draft and DocuSign link to Luminar?

Thanks — need approval by EOD Friday to meet their procurement timing.

—Alex
